summary: Not a Medium clone: the readership is the product and no code produces it. This is the consolation done right: your archive imported to your own domain, a typographic reading experience, syndication to Medium with canonical pointing home so the audience still finds you, and a reader list you own.

stack.choice: Any static host on your domain

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your Medium export
prerequisites.why: Phase 1 imports every past post with its date.
prerequisites.get: Medium > Settings > Security and apps > Download your information. You receive a zip of HTML files by email.

prerequisites.name: A static host connected to the repo
A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: A Medium integration token (optional)
prerequisites.why: Phase 3 syndicates with canonical set. Medium's API is limited; the import-a-story tool is the fallback.
prerequisites.get: Medium > Settings > Security and apps > Integration tokens. If unavailable, use medium.com/p/import with your post URL.

env.name: MEDIUM_TOKEN
env.where: Integration token for syndication. Empty means use the import tool by hand.

phases.title: Your archive
phases.goal: Every past post on your domain with its original date.

steps.do: Create the Astro project and a posts collection with validated frontmatter
commands: npm create astro@latest archive -- --template minimal --typescript strict --install --git

steps.do: Convert the export's HTML to Markdown with original dates and canonical fields
Add index, tag pages, RSS with full content and a sitemap

check: Every past post renders with its original date

phases.title: Reading experience
phases.goal: Typography worth reading, zero client JavaScript.

steps.do: Layout with a measured line length, dark mode, reading time, heading anchors
Run Lighthouse and fix what it names

phases.title: Syndication with canonical
phases.goal: Publish here first, mirror to Medium with canonical home.

steps.do: Write scripts/syndicate.mjs using the integration token with canonicalUrl, or document the import tool
steps.detail: The reverse order leaves Medium canonical; do not do it.

steps.do: Mirror one post and verify canonical in the page source on Medium

check: A post published on your domain appears on Medium with canonical pointing home

phases.title: Readers you own
phases.goal: A signup list stored locally, exported into a sender when ready.

steps.do: One small Node endpoint with honeypot and rate limit storing to SQLite
A form on every post and a CSV export

phases.title: Deploy

steps.do: README: publish-here-first rule, the import path, the signup export

check: A new post is live and mirrored
The README states the canonical rule

phases.title: Operate the signup endpoint
phases.goal: Monitor and back up the one server you run.

steps.do: Nightly backup off the box and one restore

check: An alert fires when the endpoint stops

product.outcome: An archive that outlives any platform, with the audience rented by canonical syndication rather than owned by Medium.

architecture.swap: Add other platforms with the same rule

operations.backup: The repo; the signup database nightly.

releaseGate: One restore of the signup database

notIncluded: The recommendation feed, claps, publications, Partner Program earnings: that is the network.
after: Syndicate to Substack Notes or dev.to with the same rule
